statement_en: Does there exist a minimal basis with positive density, say $A\subset\mathbb{N}$, such that for any $n\in A$ the (upper) density of integers which cannot be represented without using $n$ is positive?
statement_lean:
namespace Set
open Filter
open scoped Topology
@[inline]
noncomputable abbrev partialDensity {β : Type*} [Preorder β] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β]
    (S : Set β) (A : Set β := Set.univ) (b : β) : ℝ :=
  ((S ∩ A) ∩ Iio b).ncard / (A ∩ Iio b).ncard
end Set

namespace Set
open Filter
open scoped Topology
noncomputable def upperDensity {β : Type*} [Preorder β] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β]
    (S : Set β) (A : Set β := Set.univ) : ℝ :=
  atTop.limsup fun (b : β) ↦ S.partialDensity A b
end Set

open Set
open scoped BigOperators Pointwise

def Rep (A : Set ℕ) (m h : ℕ) : Prop := m ∈ h • A

def UnrepWithout (A : Set ℕ) (n h : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {m | ¬ Rep (A \ {n}) m h}

def MinAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder (A : Set ℕ) (h : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder A h ∧ ∀ n ∈ A, ¬ IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder (A \ {n}) h

theorem erdos_52584 :
    ∃ (A : Set ℕ), ∃ h, MinAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder A h ∧
    0 < A.upperDensity ∧ ∀ n ∈ A, 0 < (UnrepWithout A n h).upperDensity := by
  sorry
